change.title: pr-6
change.description: UX: show complete URL path if website domain is same as instance domain
change.author: Arpit Jalan

findings.title: website_name leaks the website of TL0 users to anonymous viewers
findings.body: The website is hidden from anonymous viewers of trust-level-0 users: `website` is listed in `untrusted_attributes` (app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:105-111), and that macro's generated `include_website?` returns false when `scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)` (lines 25-33; the rule is in lib/guardian/user_guardian.rb:58-60). The new `website_name` is not in that list. Its own hook, `include_website_name` (line 153-155), only checks `website.present?` and never calls `restrict_user_fields?`. So for an anonymous request for a TL0 profile the serialized user still carries `website_name` (the host, plus path when the domains match). This reaches the page too: app/controllers/users_controller.rb:33 and :50-51 preload the same JSON into the HTML, and app/assets/javascripts/discourse/templates/user/user.hbs:66-73 renders `model.website_name` as a plain span (no href, because `website` is omitted). The existing spec (spec/serializers/user_serializer_spec.rb:13-15) only checks the untrusted list, so it still passes. Also, the method is named `include_website_name` without `?`, unlike every other include hook in this file, so it is not the hook the serializer consults for `website_name`; the presence check never runs and the key is emitted as null for users with no website. Fix: delete lines 153-155 and add `:website_name` to the `untrusted_attributes` list (lines 105-111). That generates `include_website_name?` with both the restriction and the presence check.

findings.title: Websites that URI() rejects lose their name silently
findings.body: `URI(website.to_s).host rescue nil` returns nil for any value Ruby's URI parser rejects, and line 140 then returns nil. Values with non-ASCII characters (for example an IDN such as http://bücher.de) or with spaces raise URI::InvalidURIError. The profile stores whatever was typed: app/services/user_updater.rb:105-106 only prefixes 'http://' when the value does not already start with 'http'. The old client code split the string on '/' (the removed `websiteName` in the controller), which did show these hosts. With this change the website name disappears from the header for those users, with no error and no fallback. Fix: when URI raises, fall back to the authority part of the raw string (for example the text between '://' and the next '/', '?' or '#') instead of returning nil. Confidence is medium because the parser behaviour is Ruby stdlib, which I did not run.

findings.title: Header keeps the old website name after saving preferences
findings.body: The header now reads the server-computed `model.website_name` (app/assets/javascripts/discourse/templates/user/user.hbs:66-71), while its link still reads `model.website`. Preferences bind `model.website` directly (app/assets/javascripts/discourse/templates/user/preferences.hbs:156-158), and the preferences save calls `model.save()` (app/assets/javascripts/discourse/controllers/preferences.js.es6:117). `save()` in this file (lines 206-216) sends `website` but only copies `bio_excerpt` back from the response (line 210). So after the user saves a new website, the header link points at the new URL while its text is still the old host, or the globe icon does not appear at all if the user had no website before. The header is visible on the preferences pages because they render into the `user` template's outlet (app/assets/javascripts/discourse/routes/preferences-index.js.es6:5 and routes/app-route-map.js.es6:74). The old computed property updated at once. The stale value also survives in-app navigation: the `user` route's afterModel that calls `findDetails()` (routes/user.js.es6:50-54) runs only when the route is entered, not on child transitions. The fix is to refresh `website_name` after the save, either from the PUT response or by deriving the host from `model.website` on the client again as before.

findings.title: No spec covers website_name for restricted or website-less users
findings.body: The anonymous TL0 context (lines 6-16) asserts only the `untrusted_attributes` list, so it cannot catch the website_name exposure. The 'has a website name' cases (lines 76-91) always set a website for a non-restricted viewer. There is no case for an anonymous viewer of a TL0 user (expect no website_name key), none for a user with no website (expect no website_name key, which the broken presence hook currently fails to give), and none for a website that URI() rejects. Adding `website_name` to the untrusted list in the anonymous context would fix the first gap.

findings.title: Sibling subdomains show the full path, wider than the PR title
findings.body: The PR title says the complete path is shown when the website domain is the same as the instance domain. Lines 144-146 also show the path when both hosts share a parent domain, for example blog.example.com on forum.example.com. The comment on line 145 says that is intended (www.example.com == forum.example.com), but no spec covers that branch. Is showing the path for sibling subdomains the intended behaviour?

contracts.action: Serialize website_name for every user, including anonymous viewers of TL0 profiles
contracts.equivalent_path: app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:25-33 and 105-111 (website hidden through untrusted_attributes); base controllers/user.js.es6 websiteName, which the diff removes, derived the host on the client from model.website
contracts.before_after: Before: the host was derived on the client from `website`, which is omitted for restricted viewers, so nothing showed. After: the server adds `website_name` with only a presence check, so restricted viewers receive it.
contracts.visible_effect: Anonymous visitors of TL0 profiles see the website host in the header (the template renders the value as a plain span).
contracts.failure_mode: The restriction is not applied, so the exposure is silent. A URI parse error also yields nil and hides the name silently (user_serializer.rb:138-140).

contracts.action: Save website in preferences and refresh the header
contracts.equivalent_path: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/templates/user/user.hbs (base) computed the host reactively from model.website via the controller's websiteName property
contracts.before_after: Before: the header text followed model.website at once. After: the header text comes from website_name, which the save does not update, while the href still follows model.website.
contracts.visible_effect: After saving a new website, the header link text is the old host (or the globe icon is missing) until a full page reload.
contracts.failure_mode: Silent stale display; nothing is lost on the server. The value persists in the session because the user route's afterModel does not re-run on child transitions.

contracts.action: Look up the instance hostname to compare against the website host
contracts.before_after: No change for existing paths; this is a new call into unchanged code.
contracts.visible_effect: Decides whether the header shows just the host or host plus path.

summary: Reviewed the five files in this part. The main problem is a privacy regression: `website_name` is serialized for anonymous viewers of TL0 profiles, because its include hook (user_serializer.rb:153-155) is misnamed without `?` and never calls the restriction check that hides `website`. Also: the header keeps a stale website name after saving preferences (user.js.es6:206-216 only refreshes bio_excerpt), and websites that URI() rejects, such as IDNs or values with spaces, now lose their name silently. The controller and model edits are otherwise clean. The spec has no coverage for the restricted case, and the sibling-subdomain path behaviour needs the author's confirmation.
